title: They Deleted My Account and Content - 0 Customer Service
content:
After the app's recent update, I was forced to log in again. No big deal, right? I do this all the time after updates. Wrong; I was told I wasn't registered and needed to sign up and use the free version or subscribe.

Trying different login methods (biometrics) and following the FAQs didn't help. Uninstalling, restarting, and reinstalling didn't work. I reached out to customer service, but they were skeptical and asked for proof of membership and payment. I subscribed through my Apple account and have the full subscription and payment history.

I sent many screenshots showing the active subscription, Apple receipts for the monthly charges, and screenshots of any related subscriber emails. I sent all the requested evidence and more… crickets, just crickets. No word back from them. It was, and still is, a terrible way to treat your (previously) happily paying customers.

Now I'm looking for tools with better support, or even open-source GitHub repos, to do what I want—not coming back to this.

title: I’m Fed up!
content:
⭐️ 1 Star — Extremely frustrating experience

I have spent hundreds of credits trying to get Kling to do one very specific thing: use my uploaded photo for the characters and follow the action in my uploaded reference video.

What makes this even more frustrating is that Kling has successfully made three or four videos for me before, ranging from about 10 seconds to 30 seconds long. Those videos came out correctly. I know the feature works. I know what I’m doing. I’m using the same process I’ve successfully used before.

So now I’m trying to make a simple 9-second video, and Kling repeatedly ignores the video reference and does whatever movement it decides to do. In some attempts, it essentially gives me the same image I uploaded instead of following the reference video at all.

I’ve contacted support multiple times through email, the website, the web, and the app. I’ve already gone through the complaint and troubleshooting process repeatedly. Despite all of that, the problem has not been resolved, and I have not been reimbursed for the hundreds of credits used on these failed generations.

I’m not complaining because I expect every generation to be perfect. I understand AI can make mistakes. But I’ve already successfully created three or four videos with Kling using this process. I know it can work, and I know I’m not doing something wrong.

That’s why it’s especially frustrating to keep losing credits on a 9-second video that isn’t even following the reference I’m providing.

I’ve given Kling multiple opportunities to address this through every support channel available to me. At this point, I’m done wasting credits.

I know this feature works. I’ve seen it work. I just want Kling to follow the reference I’m providing instead of doing whatever it wants with my credits.

title: They charge YOU for THEIR mistakes.
content:
The problem isn’t that the AI makes mistakes. Every AI does. The problem is who pays for those mistakes.

I subscribed, crafted a detailed, high-quality prompt, and generated my first video. The result wasn’t just different from what I envisioned…it barely resembled the instructions I had given. So I did what any reasonable customer would do: I refined the prompt and tried again. Then again. And again. Five generations later, despite substantially changing the prompt each time, the output remained remarkably similar, repeating many of the same shortcomings while quietly draining my credits.

When I contacted support, this was their response:

“Credits are only refunded for failed generations (such as technical errors or system failures). If the generation completes but does not meet your expectations or the prompt directions, credits are not automatically refunded. This is because credits are deducted for every successful generation, regardless of the content quality or user satisfaction.”

Read that last sentence again:

“Regardless of the content quality or user satisfaction.”

That isn’t just disappointing…it’s revealing.

To the customer, a successful generation is one that reasonably follows the prompt. To Kling AI, a successful generation is simply one that didn’t crash the server. Those are two entirely different definitions of “success,” and only one of them is coming out of my wallet.

Imagine hiring an artist to paint your portrait. They hand you a picture of someone else and say, “Well… the paint dried successfully. That’ll be full price.”

Technically, a painting was produced. Practically, the job wasn’t done.

Creative AI is inherently experimental. Everyone understands that. But when every experiment costs the customer money…especially when the model repeatedly ignores the prompt…the financial risk is shifted entirely onto YOU while KLINGAI profits from every attempt. Whether intentional or not, that’s a business model that rewards volume over reliability.

Here’s the irony: the better the AI becomes, the fewer generations users need. A pricing structure that profits from repeated failed attempts creates incentives that are difficult to ignore and even harder for customers to trust.

There are far better ways to build customer loyalty:

* Include several free rerolls for the same prompt.
* Refund credits when the output clearly fails to follow major prompt instructions.
* Charge only when a user chooses to keep or export a generation.
* Use a hybrid system where customers aren’t penalized for obvious prompt-following failures.

Those approaches would align the company’s incentives with the customer’s: produce better results, not simply more generations.

I don’t expect perfection from AI.

I do expect a company to value content quality and user satisfaction…especially when those are the very reasons customers are paying in the first place.

I’m paying for a creative tool.

I’m not paying tuition for someone else’s AI.
✌️

title: Paying Customers Are Losing Credits on Broken Generations
content:
I would like to provide feedback regarding Kling video generation.

I am a paying customer and regularly generate story-based videos with recurring characters for content creation. My biggest concern is not generation speed or resolution, but consistency and usable output. Many generations contain significant errors that force me to discard large portions of the video, including:

* Character appearance changing during the clip.
* Objects changing size or position.
* Characters dropping items they were supposed to hold.
* Instructions being ignored despite being clearly stated.
* Unwanted actions being introduced into the scene.
* Inconsistent continuity between the starting and ending frames.

Because of these issues, I often have to trim away a large percentage of the generated footage. While I may pay for a 15-second generation, only a portion of that footage is usable in the final edit.

I also have concerns about branding and value. As a paying customer, I am effectively showcasing Kling-generated content to my audience whenever the Kling branding is visible on generated videos. If I am paying for generations and helping increase visibility of the platform through my published content, I would like to see greater value returned through improved generation reliability, reduced token loss from failed generations, or additional benefits for paying creators.

As a paying customer, I would like to see improvements in:

* Character consistency.
* Object consistency.
* Instruction adherence.
* Continuity between keyframes.
* Reliability of generated actions.
* Better value for creators when generations contain significant errors.

These improvements would provide much greater value than simply increasing generation length or resolution.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

title: Racial Bias Against Blacks and Blue Collar Workers. Classist Also
content:
Kling AI has incredible potential—the visuals are stunning and the possibilities for creators are endless. But let me be very clear: the racial bias embedded in this platform is unacceptable. As a Black creator, I am outraged at how poorly Black people and Black hair are represented. Requests for natural Black features are constantly minimized, distorted, or whitewashed. In 2025, there is no excuse for an “advanced” AI to keep repeating the same harmful biases we’ve been fighting for decades.

On top of that, I am shocked at the constant injection of unwarranted Chinese symbolism into my generated content—despite never asking for it. This feels like cultural propaganda baked into a tool that should be neutral and user-driven. Developers, this is insulting and undermines the authenticity of my work.

To the Kling team: you’ve built something with world-class potential, but your neglect of inclusivity and neutrality is a massive failure. Black people, Black hair, and our culture must be respected—not erased, distorted, or overwritten with irrelevant symbolism. Fix this. Now!

~King Arod Eternal (Kingofdigitalverse)

title: My Favorite app for AI Pictures & Video
content:
OK, I am one of those alien people who actually reads the Terms of Service when possible - if there’s a chance I may use something potentially proprietary for business.  My primary use of the software is personal (an online community that does tons of AI) but I also like to create GIFS and sometimes take on graphic design work as part of my business. So I started there.

Right away I was impressed by the clarity of rules about personal and business use, as well as their general respect for rights - given that, despite some popular opinions, *even AI* image creation can result from of a substantial investment of both time and money.

I do spend money on this app, but in my opinion, it is worth every penny.  It’s head and shoulders above most of the AI image apps I’ve used. I think of it as a commercial grade product.

And in the months since I started using it, they’ve made significant improvements to an already fantastic app.

In fact, I’m pretty sure there are features I haven’t tried yet, even though I suspect that I’ve used the app for no less than 40 or 50 hours.

But the quality of the images is what prompted me to write this review.  I take my time to write reviews, so I don’t write a lot of them.

There have been a few times when they have created an image that is so beautiful it surpassed my imagination, improved on my idea & completely blew me away.

Their images have brought joy to my friends & formed the basis for awesome GIFS. In the future, I’m likely to use their images for clients. It’s quick and efficient and incredibly high-quality.

I’ve done graphic arts work on and off for more than two decades - so I can be demanding of my apps. I also know how long it might take to create anything comparable to some of these images.

But it does it in a fraction of the time & I am consistently blown away by the quality.

And the app keeps getting better.

I’m not saying that it doesn’t have the same strange glitches as all other AI apps. I have grown accustomed to what I think of as the occasional “three-arm” mistake as the current state of AI technology.  I literally can’t even remember the last time I encountered that on here, but it’s not without some of the same glitches that you find across all AI images.

I just seem to encounter them far less frequently.

Far more often than not, it delivers images that surpass all of my expectations.

In my opinion, this app is superior and amazing.

The community of other AI artists sharing their work is possibly a bit smaller than others seem, but the quality of work is ridiculous. It’s just amazing.

And switching between AI generated pictures and video is often worth every penny because the videos can be very high-quality also.  It seems like there are people using it to make very short films.

I have encountered a few AI typical strange AI glitches in video.  To the best of my recollection, they weren’t the three-arms kind of glitch, as much as slight changes to a person‘s face at certain angles when I tried to make much longer or more elaborate videos.  That happened a small handful of times out of the many hours I’ve spent on the app — and it was after they took an uploaded still picture of a person‘s face and created a believable enough video out of it that I kept wanting to extend it. The technology is extraordinary.

I’ve gone through thousands of apps on my iPhone & iPad. This is one of my favorites, by far.

Thank you to the company that created it. And thank you for being very fair & reasonable about users rights.

One final thought – The three arms type of glitches have never bothered me enough to report them or ask for credit. So I have no idea if that’s a possibility on this app.

To the best of my recollection, they weren’t the three-arms kind of glitch, as much as slight changes to a person‘s face at certain angles when I tried to make much longer or more elaborate videos.  That happened a small handful of times out of the many hours I’ve spent on the app — and it was after they took an uploaded still picture of a person‘s face and created a believable enough video out of it that I kept wanting to extend it. The technology is extraordinary.

I’ve gone through thousands of apps on my iPhone & iPad. This is one of my favorites, by far.

Thank you to the company that created it. And thank you for being very fair & reasonable about users rights.

One final thought – The three arms type of glitches have never bothered me enough to report them or ask for credit. So I have no idea if that’s a possibility on this app.
